result.text: Statistically significant reduction in HAE attacks per 4 weeks: donidalorsen-4 LS mean 0.44 vs placebo 2.26 (81% reduction, 95% CI 65%, 89%); donidalorsen-8 LS mean 1.02 (55% reduction, 95% CI 22%, 74%)

citations.quote: Trial CS5 met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks in the donidalorsen-4 group (least squares [LS] mean =0.44, 95% CI =0.27, 0.73) and the donidalorsen-8 group (LS mean =1.02, 95% CI =0.65, 1.59), compared to the pooled placebo group (LS mean =2.26, 95% CI =1.66, 3.09); this represents a percentage reduction in the means relative to placebo for the donidalorsen-4 group of 81% (95% CI =65%, 89%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group of 55% (95% CI =22%, 74%).

indication.text: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older

citations.quote: DAWNZERA™ is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.

target_moa.text: GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide that binds prekallikrein (PKK) mRNA, causing RNase H1-mediated degradation and reduced PKK production, thereby reducing downstream bradykinin, the main mediator of angioedema in HAE

citations.quote: Mechanism of action	Donidalorsen is an ASO-GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through binding to PKK mRNA, which results in reduced production of PKK protein. PKK is mainly synthesized by the liver and it is a pro-enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE.

Donidalorsen inhibits production of prekallikrein, a key protein in the contact/kallikrein-kinin system pathway that is primarily synthesized in the liver, thereby reducing the downstream production of bradykinin, the main mediator of angioedema in HAE.
Donidalorsen is a new molecular entity, first-in-class chimeric GalNAc-conjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl-modified antisense oligonucleotide targeting prekallikrein mRNA.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%): injection site reactions (24% Q4W), upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, abdominal discomfort. Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject; decreases in platelet count and increases in liver enzymes observed.

As with other GalNac-ASOs, effects on clinical laboratory results including decreased platelet counts, increased liver enzymes, and an increase in international normalized ratio (INR) were observed, but these did not result in a safety signal in terms of adverse events.
